title: WALTEUR reconstructed-intent frontmatter
description: Machine-checkable portion of walteur-kit/INTENT.md (the COMPREHEND-phase contract, §2.6 BROWNFIELD UPGRADE). The symmetric twin of prd.schema.json: where a PRD declares the intent of a NEW build, INTENT reverse-engineers the intent of an EXISTING one — what the app IS, the ORIGINAL goal it was built for, what it is USED for, and who uses it. Every claim is labeled confirmed (grounded in code/docs/commits at a file:line) / inferred (a reasoned best guess) / unknown (needs Tony). Lets intent-reconstruction-gate.sh do a zero-dep structural check and anchors the §5.5 intended-vs-implemented audit to the reconstructed intent. Markets/segments are problems/jobs, never demographics; timeframes are relative, never dates.

date.description: run-date YYYY-MM-DD the reconstruction was performed

reconstructed.description: true = reverse-engineered from the code/docs/history; false = read from an existing walteur-kit/PRD.md (the short-circuit path for a WALTEUR-built app)

what_it_is.description: the system's identity in one or two sentences — what kind of thing it is

original_goal.description: the ORIGINAL goal it was built to serve — the problem it set out to solve, reconstructed from evidence (README, commit messages, code shape) not invented

used_for.description: what it is USED for today — the jobs it actually does for its users

users.description: who uses it, framed as jobs/situations (not demographics)

claims.description: the reconstruction, claim by claim — the discipline that separates grounded fact from hallucinated guess. Every load-bearing statement about the app carries a confidence label; confirmed claims MUST cite evidence (file:line / path / commit).

statement.description: the claim about the app (a feature, a goal, a constraint, a design decision)

label.description: confirmed = grounded in evidence at a file:line; inferred = a reasoned guess from the code shape; unknown = needs Tony to confirm

evidence.description: REQUIRED when label=confirmed — a file:line, path, commit hash, or doc reference grounding the claim. Absence on a confirmed claim is a reconstruction failure (a guess dressed as a fact).

success_metrics.description: the implicit success metrics the app was optimizing for, reconstructed where evident; each carries a number+unit where known

open_questions.description: the unknowns the reconstruction could NOT settle from evidence — the [HUMAN/EXPERT REVIEW REQUIRED] list Tony must confirm before an upgrade that depends on them

evidence_refs.description: the corpus the reconstruction read — README/docs, package manifests, key source files, git history — as file:line or path refs. Grounds the whole artifact: an INTENT with no evidence_refs is a hallucination.
